items.page_evidence: Line 1 says the network exchanges two banks with prescribed signs and restores every auxiliary value it uses. Line 15 says a route applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}, that scratch roles have rho(w)=w with sign +1, and that every role, auxiliary roles included, keeps the endpoint operator (quoting the paper).
items.paper_evidence: Lines 120-122 say the network restores every auxiliary value; lines 146-148, in the same paragraph, say that undoing the exchange and signs leaves the endpoint operator on every role array, including the roles that carried auxiliary scalar values. Lines 728-737 (Lemma scalar-motifs) give restoration of auxiliary scalar values. Lines 822-823: all roles, including auxiliary roles, enter the frame identity. Lines 1169-1171: every non-X role has zero source matrix and identity sink matrix, so its endpoint difference is I_m. Lines 1531-1533: the result is H<-H+D on every original row, including rows assigned to scratch roles.
items.reason: Restoration is a property of the scalar network's values, while the endpoint operator is the frame action on each role's address-indexed array; the paper asserts both side by side, so the page is consistent. The paper needs scratch-role rows to receive the shear (they hold genuine data rows), and their endpoint difference is I_m, not the identity, so the note's proposed hypothesis that auxiliary source and sink frames coincide would contradict the construction. The quoted statement is correct.

items.page_evidence: Line 7 defines an index as iota=(T_1,T_2,T_3) in T^3, an ordered triple of triples; line 11 sets N=binom(h,3)^3 as the number of indices.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 654-660: v=binom(h,3)=161700, N=v^3=4227952113000000, and the banks X_a, Y_a are indexed by a=(a_1,a_2,a_3) in T^3. Lines 1162-1164: one negative source projection per X_a, N in all. Line 1107: the ratio L_b/N=100/539 uses N=v^3.
items.reason: Indices are ordered elements of T^3 (one triple per tensor coordinate), not 3-element sets of triples, so their number is binom(h,3)^3 exactly as the page says; 161700^3 matches the paper's N. The note's binom(binom(h,3),3) counts unordered sets, which the construction does not use, and the signed total WD-2N is unaffected.

items.page_evidence: Line 13 defines Q_k as the time per unit volume for interchanging fields of m^k bits; line 11 says each of the s calls acts on a role stream of volume V/W; line 15 concludes that a field of u=m^k bits has Q_k=O(u^tau) and the interchange costs O(Vu^tau).
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1481-1488 (Prop. power-interchange) prove O(Ve^tau) for e=m^k under a row field of length divisible by W^k; lines 1552-1557 give the recurrence and F_k=O(e^tau). Lines 1631-1645 (Lemma chunk-swap) remove the width and row restrictions and give O(Vu^tau) for arbitrary arrays and widths.
items.reason: The quoted statement is explicitly restricted to u=m^k, so the objection that the recurrence covers only powers of m misreads it. The conclusion that interchanging such fields costs O(Vu^tau) is true in the paper without any row hypothesis (Lemma chunk-swap), and it follows from the page's own recurrence; the row field is a hypothesis of the paper's intermediate proposition, i.e. of how the recurrence is realized, not of the stated result. That the page does not mention the extension lemma is an exposition point.

items.page_evidence: Line 13: the edge operators telescope and the route applies only its endpoint operator D_{alpha_k}D_{alpha_0}^{-1}. Line 15: the route applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}, and multiplying by eps_w removes the sign; every role keeps the endpoint operator. Line 17: with source frame I and sink frame D_nu, its operator is D_nu, however many gates it passes through.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 143-146: a route applies D_sink D_source^{-1}, together with its prescribed scalar sign (sign kept separate). Lines 820-822: the route applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}. Lines 1279-1282: an input role reaches its output with that sign and with operator C_sink C_source^{-1} (operator named without the sign); lines 1284-1286 by contrast speak of the route operator multiplied by its sign.
items.reason: The example illustrates the telescoping of frames ('however many gates'), and 'its operator' reads naturally as the endpoint (frame) operator D_nu I^{-1}=D_nu, which is how line 13 and the paper at 1279-1282 use the word, with the scalar sign treated separately. Read as the full route action of line 15, it would be -D_nu when eps_w=-1, so a strict reader can see a tension; that ambiguity in the word 'operator', which the paper shares, makes this borderline rather than a clear misstatement.

items.page_evidence: Line 7 defines labels as nondegenerate subspaces of F=(Q^h)^{tensor 3}, notes neighbors are orthogonal, and says that along a side wire a label containing t_T may grow to t_S^perp, adding h-2 dimensions.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 944-953: suppressing the factor Q, on a side wire joining neighbors t_X, t_Y the remaining component passes P tensor <t_X> inside P tensor t_Y^perp inside P tensor F; the first inclusion holds because t_X is orthogonal to t_Y. Lines 1038 and 1056-1058: side edge 2->5 has residual P tensor <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2.
items.reason: The mathematics is right: on the exposed tensor factor, <t_T> lies in t_S^perp by orthogonality, and the growth from dimension 1 to h-1 adds h-2, which is also the dimension added in F because P and Q are lines. The page suppresses the line factors P and Q (as the paper itself suppresses Q at line 944), so the sentence is loosely typed with respect to its own definition of a label; whether that is an acceptable informal shorthand or a misstatement is a matter of judgement.

items.page_evidence: Line 1 calls tau 'the fixed exponent below 1'; line 11 says only 'fix tau<1 with s/W<m^tau'; line 15 handles the case s/W<=1 by bounding the geometric sum by k and asserts k=O(m^{k tau}) 'since m>=2'. m is never introduced on the page.
items.paper_evidence: Line 1481 (Prop. power-interchange): choose tau in (0,1) with s/W<m^tau. Lines 1554-1556: if a<=1 the sum is at most k+1=O(m^{k tau}), which uses tau>0. Lines 1340-1343 and 1633: 0<tau<1 throughout. Line 1451: m,W>=2.
items.reason: k=O(m^{k tau}) needs m^tau>1, i.e. tau>0 as well as m>=2; the page's only constraint on tau is tau<1 and s/W<m^tau, which in the case s/W<1 that the page explicitly treats admits tau<0, where the claim (and Q_k=O(u^tau)) fails. The paper requires tau in (0,1) exactly here, so the page drops a hypothesis the step uses. It is borderline because tau>0 is arguably implicit in a power-saving exponent and the degenerate case never arises for the actual network, where s/W is close to m.

items.page_evidence: Line 13 says the route applies only its endpoint operator D_{alpha_k}D_{alpha_0}^{-1}; line 15 says the route applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1} and that undoing the sign leaves the endpoint operator; line 17 gives the example with source frame I and sink frame D_nu, operator D_nu.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 143-146: the route applies D_sink D_source^{-1} together with its prescribed scalar sign. Lines 820-822: eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}. Lines 1279-1282: 'with that sign and with operator C_sink C_source^{-1}', where 'operator' excludes the sign.
items.reason: Same quoted statement as R04. The example concerns cancellation of intermediate frames, and 'its operator' as the sign-free endpoint operator D_nu is consistent with line 13 and with the paper's own usage at 1279-1282; it is wrong only if 'operator' is read as the full signed route action of line 15 with eps_w=-1. The note's mathematics is correct under that reading, so the verdict is borderline.

items.page_evidence: Line 19: m=2, s=3, W=2, s/W=3/2, log_2(3/2)~0.585, and for lambda=0.8 the ratio (3/2)/2^{0.8}~0.86. Line 13 defines the ratio as (s/W)/m^lambda.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 2416-2419: the internal costs are a geometric series in a/m^lambda with a=s/W<m^lambda, which is the page's ratio; the example itself is the page's own.
items.reason: 2^{0.8}=e^{0.8 ln 2}~e^{0.5545}~1.741, and 1.5/1.741~0.862, so the page's value 0.86 is correct. The note computes 1.5/1.74 as 1.16, which is wrong; the example is consistent with lambda=0.8>log_2(3/2) giving a ratio below 1.

items.page_evidence: Line 5: the updates are D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D, the middle one being the address shear; the outer two cost linear time.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1539-1540: only the middle shear uses the circuit; the other two updates target the later group and have linear cost. Lines 1399-1400: every H_i precedes every D_j. Lines 1357-1358 and 555-571 (Lemma ordered-affine-streams): a later field can be updated by a fixed linear combination of earlier fields, and multiplied by a rational unit such as -1, in O(V).
items.reason: The statement is exactly the paper's. The outer updates change the later field D using the earlier field H, which a controlled cyclic shift does in linear time; the middle update changes the earlier field H by the later field D, which is the costly direction on tape. The note's claim that the two kinds of update are equivalent ignores this order asymmetry; the page not explaining it is not a misstatement.

items.page_evidence: Line 9: along an edge from alpha to beta the stored array changes by D_beta D_alpha^{-1}. Line 13 writes the route product with the last edge's factor leftmost and the first edge's factor rightmost.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 806-816: the invariant carries D_u phi to D_v phi on each edge, and the implemented operator is D_out S D_in^{-1}; lines 143-145 and 820-822: the route applies D_sink D_source^{-1}.
items.reason: With operators acting on the left of an array, the rightmost factor acts first, so writing the first edge's factor D_{alpha_1}D_{alpha_0}^{-1} on the right is the correct composition order. Adjacent factors then meet as D_{alpha_j}^{-1}D_{alpha_j} and cancel, giving D_{alpha_k}D_{alpha_0}^{-1} with no commutativity needed. The note reverses the convention.

items.page_evidence: Line 9: the outside work is a fixed number of address-field row additions; Omega is the bit count of one axis chunk, eta>0 fixed with Omega<=d^eta; a row addition on fields of u=f Omega bits costs O(V(u^tau+1)).
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1974-2010 (Lemma packed-selected-bit-rectangle): a row addition y_{j_i}<-y_{j_i}+x_{j_i} at selected positions j_i=rho+iK of L=fK-bit chunks costs the explicit bound at line 2003, which simplifies to O(V(L^tau+1)) only when A_rect=O(p), R exceeds every fixed polynomial in p, f<=d<=p and K/log p->infinity (lines 2007-2010). Lines 2291-2300: each slot has (e/m)K address bits, so the lemma gives the stated bound for a row addition, and the number of row additions is fixed. Lines 1781-1792 set the standing parameter family.
items.reason: The page's 'row addition on fields of u=f Omega bits' matches the paper's own use of 'row addition' for the packed selected-bit addition on slots of (e/m)K bits, so the note is wrong that the page claims addition of two u-bit integers, and its complaints about missing reasons are exposition points. What holds is that the bound is the lemma's asymptotic simplification, valid only in the paper's standing parameter family, which the page does not state; since the paper itself applies it at line 2297 under those standing assumptions without restating them, this is a summary-level simplification rather than a clear misstatement.

items.page_evidence: Lines 5-7: the updates D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D take (H,D) to (H,D-H), (D,D-H), (D,H), since H+(D-H)=D and D-(D-H)=H; the F_2 example (1,0)->(1,1)->(0,1)->(0,1) is checked.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1494-1495: H and D are vectors over Z/q^b Z with q an odd prime. Lines 1535-1541: the same three updates, componentwise, send (H,D) to (D,H) over that ring.
items.reason: The third update sets D to (current H)-(current D)=D-(D-H), which equals H in every abelian group, not only in characteristic 2; the note confuses this with D+(D-H). The paper uses the identity over Z/q^b Z with q odd, so it is not restricted to F_2. The quoted identities are correct.

items.page_evidence: Line 3: q is a fixed odd prime. Line 5: an entry mu/xi requires q not to divide xi and acts as mu xi^{-1} mod q^b; 'So q divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.' Line 7 then factors M=F_1 Pi F_2 and line 11 uses F_1, F_2 and their inverses.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1413-1423 (proof of Lemma matrix-shear): the factors and their inverses are put in a finite table, and q is chosen to avoid every denominator in the table and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor; a prime exceeding all nonzero numerators and denominators is given only as an example that suffices. Lines 1479-1480: q also avoids denominators of the vertex matrices.
items.reason: The sentence is presented as a consequence ('So') of the requirement that q not divide denominators, but avoiding numerators does not follow from that, and avoiding the denominators of M does not control the denominators of F_1, F_2 and their inverses, which must be imposed on the choice of q; this is case (b). Read literally it is also false, since a zero entry has numerator 0, which q divides (the page's own example matrix has zero entries); the paper speaks of nonzero numerators. The note's account (an extra condition on q relative to the finitely many factors, not a consequence) is correct.

items.page_evidence: Line 9: the outside work per volume is O(f^lambda) when lambda>tau(1+eta/vartheta), with eta>0 only said to be fixed. Line 13: the ratio is (s/W)/m^lambda. Line 15: taking lambda with log_m(s/W)<lambda<1 makes the ratio below 1, so the internal sum is at most a constant times f^lambda. Line 17 adds sigma<lambda.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 2394-2399: the paper chooses 0<tau<1, max{0,log_m(s/W)}<=sigma<1, max{tau,sigma}<lambda<1 and tau(1+c/beta)<lambda; lines 2413-2419 use these. Lines 2594-2599 make the same conditions hypotheses of Prop. simultaneous-layer, and lines 4011-4021 fix c=2^{-56} so that tau(1+c/beta)<lambda<1.
items.reason: The quoted claim is correct: lambda>log_m(s/W) is equivalent to m^lambda>s/W, i.e. ratio below 1. The other conditions on lambda are on the page (lambda>tau(1+eta/vartheta) at line 9, which implies lambda>tau; sigma<lambda at line 17). The real gap the note finds is elsewhere: the page never requires eta small enough that tau(1+eta/vartheta)<1, so these conditions together might admit no lambda<1. Because this sentence can be read as the page's full choice of lambda, the verdict is borderline.

items.page_evidence: Line 7: 'Elimination proves this: pivot on the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clear its left and lower entries by lower-triangular operations, and repeat on what remains.'
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1376-1382 (proof of Lemma lower-lower): choose the topmost nonzero row and its rightmost NONZERO entry; there are then no nonzero entries to its right in the pivot row, so clearing to the left by right multiplication with lower triangular elementary matrices suffices.
items.reason: As written the pivot is the row's rightmost entry, which can be zero (row (1,0)), and then neither pivoting nor the claim that only left and lower entries need clearing works; the choice of the rightmost nonzero entry is exactly what makes the column operations lower triangular. The note's main point holds; its complaint that the sketch is brief is only exposition. Borderline because a reader may take 'pivot' to imply a nonzero entry and silently supply the word.

items.page_evidence: Line 17: s_b=W_b R-N+2L_b, the paper shows N>2L_b, so s_b<W_b R; 'Per wire, the interchanges are fewer than R, which the recurrence turns into a saving'.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1149-1152 and 1167: s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m with deficit N-2L_b>0. Lines 1013 and 1031-1041: a central wire at stage j has edge ranks (a-1)h, h, h, h and ah(f-1) with a=h^{j-1}, f=h^{3-j}, totalling m+2h>m, so individual wires can exceed m. Lines 1552-1557: the recurrence uses only the ratio s/W.
items.reason: Immediately after s_b<W_b R, 'per wire' reads naturally as the rate s_b/W_b<R, which is true and is exactly what the recurrence uses. Read as a bound for each wire it would be false (central wires carry m+2h), so the note's correction to 'on average' is accurate about the mathematics; whether 'per wire' already means that is a matter of reading, hence borderline.

items.page_evidence: Line 5: q must not divide the denominator xi of an entry; 'So q divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.' Line 7 introduces invertible lower-triangular factors F_1, F_2; line 11 applies F_1, F_2 and their inverses modulo q^b.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1413-1423: q avoids every denominator in the finite table of factors and inverses and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor, so that the triangular factors remain invertible modulo q^b; a prime exceeding all nonzero numerators and denominators is offered only as a sufficient example. Lines 1478-1480: q as in that lemma, also avoiding vertex-matrix denominators.
items.reason: Same quoted statement as R13: it is presented as following from the denominator condition, which it does not (case b), and literally it fails for zero entries, whose numerator 0 is divisible by q. The note is right that the paper's actual requirement is avoidance of all denominators in the factor table plus numerators of diagonal entries, with 'avoid all numerators and denominators' only a sufficient choice, and that the page never says why F_1, F_2 stay invertible mod q^b; that last point alone would be exposition, but the non sequitur makes the alarm genuine.

items.page_evidence: Line 11: 'fix tau<1 with s/W<m^tau', with no lower bound on tau. Line 15: if s/W<=1 the sum is at most k; 'Both are O(m^{k tau}), since m>=2.' The page never defines m or states m>=2.
items.paper_evidence: Line 1481: tau in (0,1) with s/W<m^tau. Lines 1554-1556: for a<=1 the sum is at most k+1=O(m^{k tau}). Lines 1343 and 1633: 0<tau<1. Line 1451: fix integers m,W>=2.
items.reason: Same step as R06: k=O(m^{k tau}) requires tau>0 as well as m>=2, the page's choice of tau allows tau<0 when s/W<1, and the paper requires tau in (0,1). The note's point that m>=2 is never stated on the page is true but is only an exposition gap (the paper fixes m>=2 and the network has m=10^6). Borderline because tau>0 is arguably implicit and the case is degenerate for the actual network.

items.page_evidence: Line 3: 'A recursive call at parameter mf makes s subcalls at parameter f, each on a stream of volume V/W.' Line 5: V is the volume a call works on. The linked linear-network page explains padding row counts to multiples of W so that each role stream holds V/W bits.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 170-171 (overview) state verbatim that a call at mf uses s calls at f, each on a stream of volume V/W, with V the node volume after padding (lines 125-128). Lines 1482-1484 and 1500-1502 (power-width proposition) assume a row field divisible by W^k so each stream has volume exactly V/W; lines 2306-2342 pad once at the root to a multiple of W^{k_0} so child volumes are exactly V/W at every depth.
items.reason: The statement is the paper's own overview statement and is true of the recursion as the paper sets it up, where rows are supplied and padded once at the root so every split is exact. The divisibility hypothesis is a technical precondition the page leaves implicit; without it, padding at each level could make subcall volumes exceed V/W, so a strict reader can call the claim under-hypothesised. The note's complaint about why the parameter is a power of m is only exposition. Borderline.
